entry_points.name: delete_account
entry_points.note: Reachable at accounts/<int:pk>/delete/ and calls Account.delete() on the row named by the URL.

entry_points.name: admin.site.register
entry_points.note: Account is registered in the Django admin, so an operator can delete rows from the admin change list.

stores.name: accounts_account

fields.name: joined_at
fields.note: Records when this person's account row was created.

erasure.note: The delete_account view loads the Account row and calls delete() on it, which removes the row.

stores.note: The subject table: one row per account holder.

stores.name: account.avatar

fields.name: avatar
fields.note: An uploaded image of the account holder, stored under account/avatars/ outside the database row.

erasure.note: Deleting the Account row fires a post_delete receiver registered with sender=Account that calls avatar.delete(save=False); the receiver module is imported in AccountsConfig.ready().

stores.note: The image file behind the Account.avatar field, which lives in storage rather than in the table.

stores.name: accounts_comment

fields.name: body
fields.note: A free-text column the account holder writes into; the schema does not constrain what it holds.

fields.name: posted_at
fields.note: Records when this person posted the comment.

erasure.note: The foreign key to Account uses on_delete=DB_CASCADE, so the database removes the comment rows when the account row goes; no Django delete signal is sent for them, and nothing on this table depends on one.

stores.note: Comments written by an account holder, linked by the account foreign key.

stores.name: accounts_address

erasure.note: The foreign key to Account uses on_delete=models.CASCADE, so Django deletes the address rows in the same collector run as the account row.

stores.note: Postal addresses held against an account, linked by the account foreign key.
